newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines, China steer clear of Spratlys row.
newsitem.headline: Philippines, China steer clear of Spratlys row.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos and Chinese Defence Minister Chi Haotian agreed on Wednesday to strengthen their two countries' relations but steered clear of the thorny Spratly Islands dispute.

Despite speculation about the deteriorating health of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, Chi was not cutting short his Manila visit and will proceed to Jakarta on Thursday to meet his Indonesian counterpart, Philippine officials said.
"I had a very good discussion with President Ramos. We should carry our friendship for generations," Chi said, speaking through an interpreter.

Chi is to sign later on Wednesday an agreement for China to provide Philippine army engineers with dump trucks worth $3 million, Philippine Defence Secretary Renato de Villa told reporters after the Ramos-Chi meeting.
He said Ramos and Chi did not discuss the dispute over the Spratlys, a potentially oil-rich cluster of isles, reefs and shoals in the South China Sea.
The area is claimed wholly or in part by China, the Philippines, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei.
"You cannot expect the president to discuss this with a minister of their government," de Villa said.
He said the meeting touched on trade matters.
